blueprint_concepts: Angle Bisector Identification: Disambiguating acute/obtuse bisectors and bisector containing the origin.

concept_use.Angle bisectors: The centres of circles touching both lines lie on the angle bisectors; the bisector equation 8x - y - 6 = 0 is formed and intersected with the distance condition.
concept_use.Angle Bisector Identification: Disambigu: The sign test a1a2 + b1b2 < 0 (constants positive) shows the origin is in the acute angle, so the acute bisector is the one containing the origin; the side condition then picks one centre.

english: Let $L_1:4x-3y+2=0$ and $L_2:12x+5y-22=0$. A circle $C$ of radius $7$ touches both $L_1$ and $L_2$, its centre lies on the bisector of the acute angle between $L_1$ and $L_2$, and $C$ and the origin lie on opposite sides of $L_2$. Then the centre of $C$ is
hindi: माना $L_1:4x-3y+2=0$ तथा $L_2:12x+5y-22=0$ है। त्रिज्या $7$ का एक वृत्त $C$ दोनों रेखाओं $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ को स्पर्श करता है, इसका केन्द्र $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ के बीच के न्यून कोण के समद्विभाजक पर स्थित है, तथा $C$ और मूल बिन्दु $L_2$ के विपरीत ओर स्थित हैं। तब $C$ का केन्द्र है
solution: With constant terms positive: $4x-3y+2=0$, $-12x-5y+22=0$; $a_1a_2+b_1b_2=-48+15<0$, so the origin lies in the acute angle
Acute bisector = bisector containing the origin: $\dfrac{4x-3y+2}{5}=\dfrac{-12x-5y+22}{13}\Rightarrow 8x-y-6=0$
Centre $(h,8h-6)$ at distance $7$ from $L_1$: $\dfrac{|4h-24h+18+2|}{5}=7\Rightarrow|20-20h|=35\Rightarrow h=-\dfrac34$ or $\dfrac{11}{4}$
$h=\frac{11}4$: centre $\left(\frac{11}4,16\right)$, $L_2$ value $33+80-22=91>0$ while at $O$ it is $-22$: opposite sides
$h=-\frac34$: centre $(-\frac34,-12)$, $L_2$ value $-91<0$: same side as $O$, rejected
solution_full: Write both lines with positive constant terms: $L_1:4x-3y+2=0$ and $L_2:-12x-5y+22=0$.

Here $a_1a_2+b_1b_2=4(-12)+(-3)(-5)=-33<0$. So the origin lies in the acute angle between the lines, and the bisector of the angle containing the origin, $\dfrac{4x-3y+2}{5}=+\dfrac{-12x-5y+22}{13}$, is the acute-angle bisector.
Simplifying: $52x-39y+26=-60x-25y+110\Rightarrow112x-14y-84=0\Rightarrow8x-y-6=0$. (The other bisector, $x+8y-17=0$, bisects the obtuse angle.)
The centre lies on $8x-y-6=0$, say $(h,8h-6)$, and is at distance $7$ from $L_1$ (it is then automatically at distance $7$ from $L_2$):
The two candidates are $\left(-\frac34,-12\right)$ and $\left(\frac{11}{4},16\right)$, one in each of the two vertically opposite acute angles.
A circle touching $L_2$ lies on the same side of $L_2$ as its centre. $12x+5y-22$ is $-22$ at $O$, $91$ at $\left(\frac{11}4,16\right)$ and $-91$ at $\left(-\frac34,-12\right)$.
So the circle on the opposite side of $L_2$ from $O$ has centre $\left(\dfrac{11}{4},16\right)$. (The points $(9,1)$ and $(-7,3)$ are the centres on the obtuse-angle bisector.)
originality_note: New: all four centres of circles of a given radius touching two lines are on the two bisectors; the question selects one by combining the acute/obtuse test with a side condition relative to a line (way 3). Closest known: 'find the bisector of the acute angle between two lines'. Different because: the student must identify the acute bisector, then locate two centres on it and discard one by a side test; the four options are exactly the four candidate centres.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that the four candidate centres are distinct and that the two conditions leave exactly one. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising that the origin lies in the acute angle (sign test) and then choosing between the two acute-bisector centres by the side of L2.
justification: Two identification steps (acute bisector, side of a line) and a distance computation, with every distractor a genuine candidate. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q1 (L3) in the coordinate-geometry chain it needs.
